hero.title: Women's health
hero.description: Cervical cancer is preventable, and cervical screening can help protect your health. Whether you come from a different culture, speak another language, or have a diverse background, find clear information and support in a language that works for you.

essentials.label: 01 / Learn the essentials
essentials.title: A little knowledge
essentials.description: Cervical cancer starts in the cervix, but with regular screening and HPV vaccination, it can often be prevented before it starts.

vaccination.title: HPV vaccination
vaccination.description: HPV (human papillomavirus) is a common virus that can cause cervical cancer. Vaccination helps prevent HPV infection.

screening.title: Regular screening
screening.description: Finds cell changes early, when they are easier to treat and manage.

body.title: Know your body
body.description: Talk to a healthcare professional about anything that feels unusual.

screening.label: 02 / Frequently asked questions
screening.title: Clear answers for
screening.description: Knowing what to expect can make screening feel simpler. Here is the information to help you feel informed and supported.

what.title: What is cervical screening?
what.description: A quick health check for high-risk HPV and early cell changes in the cervix. Finding changes early helps prevent cervical cancer.

why.title: Why is it important?
why.description: Screening can find HPV and early cell changes before they become cancer. It is one of the best ways to protect your future health.

who.title: Who is it for?
who.description: In Australia, cervical screening is recommended for people aged 25 to 74 who have a cervix, whether or not they have had the HPV vaccine.

howOften.title: How often?
howOften.description: Most people need screening every five years. Your healthcare provider may recommend a different plan based on your result or health history.

whatHappens.title: What happens?
whatHappens.description: A small sample is collected from the cervix by a trained healthcare professional. It usually takes a few minutes, and you can ask questions at any time.

options.title: Your screening options
options.description: Choose a healthcare provider for a clinician-collected test, or ask if self-collection is available for you. Both options check for HPV.
options.findGp: Look for a GP near you
options.theNumber: See the participation number in Australia
